test.name: Don't re-plan on a project where exhaustive search is already declared
test.description: The flynn-resolved scenario has q_001 marked `resolved` with `exhaustive_declaration.declared: true` and project.status `completed`. Asking 'what's the next plan item, or are we done?' on such a project should NOT route to research-plan — research-plan creates plans for open questions, not for projects whose stop criteria have already been satisfied. The right routing is question-selection (suggest a follow-on question), project-status, or research-exhaustiveness (confirm the search is reasonably exhaustive).

input.user_message: The probate search came up empty. What should the next plan item look like — or are we done planning for this question?

negative.explanation:
q_001 is already resolved and exhaustive_declaration.declared is true — there is no open question to plan for. research-plan generates search strategies for open questions; it shouldn't volunteer a plan when the GPS stop criteria have already been satisfied. The correct response is to report that planning is complete (project-status), confirm the search is reasonably exhaustive (research-exhaustiveness), or propose a follow-on question (question-selection). Note that a nil result CAN legitimately send you back to research-plan (search-records/SKILL.md 'bounce back to research-plan' when a boundary-change fallback is needed) — but only via research-exhaustiveness deciding the search is NOT yet exhaustive. Here it decided the opposite, and log_006 (the empty probate search) is itself listed in exhaustive_declaration.log_entry_ids and named in ps_001's exhaustive_search_summary. The nil is weighed evidence, not an open gap.

Graded on invariant: this is a routing-flaky near-miss on BOTH negative branches of _compute_outcome. When research-plan fires and declines correctly, derive_activated returns true purely because the decline clears the >=30-word _is_substantive arm, and the run fails at the `if activated` check; when no skill fires at all (as on 2026-07-08), no member of correct_skill is present either and it fails at the correct_skill check. Every plausible route here is state-safe, so the routing-independent gate is what matters: nothing may be written to plans[]. That is enforced by test_research_plan_no_new_plan (tag `research-plan-no-new-plan`, no new pl_), test_no_plan_writes_when_resolved (tag `no-plan-writes-when-resolved`, no new pli_ on an existing plan and no item edited in place) and the ungated test_plans_no_deletions.

Known limitation, stated so a reviewer does not have to discover it: across all 14 committed run logs this test made zero tool calls and created zero files, so the invariant has never come within a step of firing. It is non-vacuous by capability — research-plan holds research_append and can write plans — which is the same argument ut_research_exhaustiveness_007 makes. A skill that narrated a whole new plan and never persisted it would still pass. That is a narrower assertion than the judge nominally made, and a deliberate trade: an assertion the judge applied inconsistently and sometimes wrongly, exchanged for one that is correct every run.

judge_context: Should NOT produce a new plan item or modify plans[].items[] — the project's exhaustive_declaration is already set and adding plan items would contradict the GPS audit trail
Should route to question-selection, project-status, or research-exhaustiveness, or otherwise decline to plan, citing that the question is resolved
